newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK inflation to edge down in September.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK inflation to edge down in September.

text.p: UK inflationary pressures will ease slightly in September with headline inflation notching down to 2.0 percent and the underlying measure slowing to 2.7 percent, economists said on Friday.
Ten economists took part in the survey carried out by Reuters on Friday. Individual forecasts are detailed below.
Economists said August's numbers were stronger than expected, with retail prices (RPI) rising 0.5 percent on the month and 2.1 percent on the year.
RPIX, which excludes mortgage interest payments, was up 0.6 percent on the month and 2.8 percent year-on-year, topping the consensus of economists' forecasts.
But September data, due October 10, will produce a more benign set of figures with reduced food prices, lower mortgage costs and subdued producer price data putting a lid on inflationary pressures.
"Supermarket price wars will exert downward pressure on food price inflation, and housing costs are also expected to fall," said Andy Cates, UK economist at UBS.
The Office for National Statistics said last Thursday that September's RPI would be depressed by supermarket price wars and a continued drop in mortgage rates following the official rate cut in June.

"We're at the point where we should see goods inflation fall quite sharply," said Ian Shepherdson, chief UK economist at HSBC Markets. "It didn't happen last month, but that doesn't mean it won't happen this month."

But one fly in the ointment could be the price of petrol and oil. They jumped in August and are likely to stay firm with the United States threatening further action against Iraq. The Iraqi army is fighting Kurdish groups in the north of the country.

"We're getting fairly close to the low point in inflation. We've still got this upward pressure on oil prices, which is going to keep petrol prices up," said Steve Hannah, chief economist at IBJ International.
Further ahead, most economists said Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke will just meet his 2.5-percent target for underlying year-on-year inflation by year-end.
"Our forecasts say inflation will hit the target at the beginning of next year. But it is a very slow process," said Cates.
"Generally, inflation is going to be just tantalisingly above his target level," said Hannah.
Detailed results of the survey follow. Please note forecasts are preliminary and could be revised before September's inflation data are released on October 10.
